testcase: JS resolve a dependency version conflict with a named catalog
query:
title: Use a newer dependency without changing every SDK

question: pnpm install reports that my JS SDK needs a different dependency version from other packages. I genuinely require functionality in a newer version. How should I handle this in the workspace?
ground_truth: First try to match the existing catalog version or the version used by most packages. If the newer functionality is necessary, create a new named catalog entry in pnpm-workspace.yaml, reference that catalog from the package, and run pnpm install to update dependencies and the lockfile. Do not bypass the consistency checks or force an unrelated repository-wide upgrade merely to make one package install.

testcase: JS link an unpublished local workspace library
query:
title: Depend on an unpublished library in my checkout

question: My JS SDK needs another library in the same repository that hasn't been published to npm yet. Can I use pnpm add to fetch it, or how do I link it locally?
ground_truth: For an unpublished repository library, manually add the appropriate workspace dependency entry to the consuming package's package.json and run pnpm install to link the local library. pnpm add cannot fetch a version that has never been published. Preserve the repository's workspace conventions and include the resulting pnpm-lock.yaml changes; do not create package-lock.json.

testcase: JS add a published development dependency
query:
title: Add a development dependency with the repository package manager

question: I need a published test helper as a devDependency of my JavaScript SDK package. Should I use npm install --save-dev in the package directory and include package-lock.json?
ground_truth: Use pnpm add "<package-name>" -D from the package directory, not npm install --save-dev. Use an approved compatible version when specifying one. pnpm updates package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml; include the relevant workspace lockfile changes and do not introduce package-lock.json.

testcase: JS resolve a pnpm workspace lockfile merge conflict
query:
title: Regenerate a conflicted workspace lockfile

question: My branch changes one SDK's dependencies and now conflicts with upstream main in pnpm-lock.yaml. What's the documented way to resolve that lockfile without losing my package.json changes?
ground_truth: Fetch and merge upstream main into the branch, resolve non-lockfile conflicts while preserving the intended package.json changes, restore the upstream main version of pnpm-lock.yaml, and run pnpm install to regenerate the lockfile from the merged manifests. Review and stage the regenerated lockfile. Restoring only the lockfile is not the final step; regenerating it is necessary to retain the branch's dependency changes.

testcase: JS filter a single test from PowerShell
query:
title: Run one Node test from PowerShell

question: I want only test/public/buckets.spec.ts and the test named "lists buckets" to run. My PowerShell shell is consuming the forwarded options. What command form does the JS contributor guide recommend?
ground_truth: From the package directory, use pnpm run test:node -- -- test/public/buckets.spec.ts -t "lists buckets" when PowerShell needs the double separator. The usual shell form has one separator: pnpm run test:node -- test/public/buckets.spec.ts -t "lists buckets". This filters the Node target rather than rerunning all Node and browser tests.

expected_references.title: Contributing: selecting test files and cases

testcase: JS record new tests from PowerShell
query:
title: Initialize recordings for a new package in PowerShell

question: For a new JS SDK package without assets.json, what is the correct order to initialize asset sync and record its first service tests in PowerShell? Assume the required test resources are provisioned.
ground_truth: Configure the package's documented resource and authentication environment variables. First run npx dev-tool test-proxy init from the package directory to create assets.json. After installing dependencies and building the package, set $env:TEST_MODE="record" and run pnpm test from the package directory. Record after initialization; if tests were recorded before init, record them again so they can be pushed. Review the recordings, run npx dev-tool test-proxy push, and include the updated assets.json with the test change.

expected_references.title: JS codegen testing: run tests in record mode

testcase: JS preserve a generated model name after casing changes
query:
title: Restore a released JS interface name

question: In a hypothetical TypeSpec migration, the JS API diff removes interface UrlRule and adds interface URLRule for the same model. How can the released public name be preserved just for JavaScript?
ground_truth: Apply a JS-scoped client name to the current TypeSpec model in client.tsp, for example @@clientName(URLRule, "UrlRule", "javascript"), qualified with the model's actual namespace. This restores the released exported interface name without renaming the model for every emitter. Regenerate and verify that the paired removal/addition disappears from the JS API diff; changing only generated TypeScript will not survive regeneration.

testcase: JS restore flattened properties during migration
query:
title: Keep direct property access in a migrated JS model

question: Consider a hypothetical migration where a released JS SDK exposes endpoint.region but TypeSpec generates endpoint.properties.region. The model Endpoint has a properties bag. Which JavaScript compatibility customization preserves direct access?
ground_truth: The JS migration guide restores the flattened surface with @@Azure.ClientGenerator.Core.Legacy.flattenProperty(Endpoint.properties, "javascript") in client.tsp, with the actual model namespace as needed. Its example suppresses @azure-tools/typespec-azure-core/no-legacy-usage with an SDK backward-compatibility justification. This is a targeted migration compatibility measure, not a new API design recommendation. Regenerate and check that the released direct-property API is restored.

expected_references.title: JS TypeSpec migration: removal of flattened properties

testcase: JS emitter metadata generation preserves package setup
query:
title: Regenerate source without recreating metadata

question: I'm using @azure-tools/typespec-ts and want to explicitly prevent generation of package.json, README.md, and tsconfig.json. Which emitter option controls that?
ground_truth: Set generate-metadata: false under options for @azure-tools/typespec-ts in tspconfig.yaml. The option controls generation of metadata files such as package.json, README.md, and tsconfig.json. Without an explicit value, metadata generation defaults to true when there is no package.json under package-dir. It is not the option for disabling SDK source generation or tests.

testcase: JS emitter honors TypeSpec authentication before YAML
query:
title: Choose the source of generated authentication

question: Our @azure-tools/typespec-ts project defines authentication with @useAuth and also has credential settings in tspconfig.yaml. Which source takes precedence, and what authentication types does this emitter document as supported?
ground_truth: Prefer defining authentication in TypeSpec with @useAuth; it takes precedence over the YAML credential configuration. The emitter documents Azure Key Credential and AAD token authentication as supported; other authentication must be handled manually. For YAML configuration, credential-scopes with add-credentials enables AAD token support, while credential-key-header-name with add-credentials configures API-key support.

testcase: JS restore a renamed generated operation
query:
title: Keep the released JS operation name during migration

question: In a hypothetical TypeSpec migration, a released Buckets.listChildren method becomes Buckets.getChildren with unchanged service behavior. How can the released JS method name be preserved without changing other languages?
ground_truth: Restore the JavaScript name with a JS-scoped client customization in client.tsp, such as @@clientName(Buckets.getChildren, "listChildren", "javascript"), qualified with the actual TypeSpec namespace or interface. Target the current TypeSpec operation, not a generated TypeScript method. Regenerate and verify that the released JS API is preserved; unchanged service behavior does not make removal of a callable SDK method nonbreaking.

expected_references.title: JS TypeSpec migration: operation naming changes

testcase: JS retain legacy LRO methods during migration
query:
title: Preserve begin methods in the migrated JS SDK

question: In a hypothetical migration, a released JS client exposes beginArchive and beginArchiveAndWait, but new modular TypeSpec output only exposes archive. Which compatibility setting preserves the released methods, and is it recommended for brand-new APIs?
ground_truth: For @azure-tools/typespec-ts, set compatibility-lro: true under options for that emitter in tspconfig.yaml. This restores the legacy begin* and begin*AndWait methods alongside the new method. The emitter reference marks this compatibility option deprecated; it is a migration/backward-compatibility setting, not a recommendation for new APIs. Regenerate and compare the exported API with the released SDK.

expected_references.title: JS TypeSpec migration: removal of begin LRO methods

testcase: JS select an emitter API version explicitly
query:
title: Generate the intended API version with the JS emitter

question: I'm using @azure-tools/typespec-ts on a versioned service. How do I select one API version explicitly rather than accept the default, and what other values does the option support?
ground_truth: Set api-version under options for @azure-tools/typespec-ts in tspconfig.yaml to the desired version string. The emitter defaults to the latest version and also accepts latest and all. This selects the service API version to generate; it is not the npm package version. Check the option support in the emitter version pinned by the project.
